Reproducing Porniece et al. (2025) from dandiset 001474¶

Paper. Porniece M, Baker J, Ausfahl CD, Zhang SX, Andermann ML (2025). Obesity dysregulates feeding-evoked response dynamics in hypothalamic satiety neurons. Scientific Reports 15, 35837. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-19800-2. The claims file was written from the open-access version of record (Europe PMC, PMC12521569), with the legends of Supplementary Figures 1 to 3 (Supplementary Material 1).

Dandiset. DANDI:001474, version 0.251031.1725. The paper cites no DANDI version (its data statement says the data are in the article and its supplements). This is the only published version, and the draft has the same 349 assets and size, so the published version is pinned.

What the dandiset holds. 349 NWB files, one per recording session, from 24 MC4R-Cre mice: per-trial matrices (10 s before to 50 s after the tone, 50 Hz) of the Ensure pump signal, licks, running and a Z-scored photometry signal computed by the depositors, the continuous raw 465 nm trace, and notes with diet, fasting, consumed Ensure and body weights. It has no 405 nm control trace, no trial table or tone time stamps, and no training sessions. Four files are second copies of other files.

Readings. Each claim is tested under the readings its criterion lists. Z1 and Z2 are the claims file's two Z-scorings, each with the per-mouse SD over all the mouse's recordings or over the recordings of one diet phase (Z1p, Z2p). The depositors' Z-score (Z0) and dF/F0 are shown as variants and do not decide outcomes. Nothing here is random, so no seed is needed.

The notebook reads all files in about 1.5 minutes and runs in about 2 minutes.

import time
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.stats.multicomp import pairwise_tukeyhsd

import pvh

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
pd.set_option("display.width", 220)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
pd.set_option("display.max_rows", 300)

started = time.time()
recs = pvh.load_all(workers=12)
print(f"loaded {len(recs)} files from dandiset {pvh.DANDISET_ID} version {pvh.DANDISET_VERSION} "
      f"in {time.time() - started:.0f} s")

loaded 349 files from dandiset 001474 version 0.251031.1725 in 58 s

# Everything below uses `recs`, the per-file measures returned by pvh.load_all.
sigmas = pvh.add_z(recs)
sigmas_phase = pvh.add_z(recs, mouse_of=lambda r: (r["subject"], pvh.phase_of(r)), suffix="p")
T = pvh.session_groups(recs)
U = T[~T.duplicate].copy()
R = pvh.recording_measures(recs, U)
by_path = {r["path"]: r for r in recs}

import hashlib
def digest(a):
    return hashlib.md5(np.ascontiguousarray(np.round(np.asarray(a, float), 6)).tobytes()).hexdigest()
content = pd.DataFrame([{"path": r["path"], "blob": r["blob"], "lick": digest(r["lick_1s"]),
                         "ensure": digest(r["ensure_onset"]),
                         "running": digest(r["run_signed"]["whole"]) if "run" in r else None,
                         "zscore": digest(r["z0"]["1-10"]) if "z0" in r else None,
                         "F0": digest(r["F0"]) if "F0" in r else None} for r in recs])
for col in ["lick", "running", "zscore", "F0"]:
    d = content[content[col].notna() & content[col].duplicated(keep=False)]
    print(f"Files sharing their {col} contents with another file: {len(d)}; all of them blob copies: "
          f"{bool(d.blob.duplicated(keep=False).all())}")

Four of the six ses-None files are the same blob as a dated file of the same subject (same identifier, same notes); each recording is counted once (the dated copy is kept). The other two ses-None files (MPK122 2024-02-06 and MPK143 2024-03-14, by their identifiers) have no dated copy and are kept. The lick, running, Z-score and F0 contents repeat only in the four blob copies, so no other recording was deposited twice.

Cohort 1 (60-trial sessions, January to April 2024) holds 6 NCD and 5 HFD mice, as the Fig. 1 legend says. Cohort 2 (90-trial sessions, July to December 2024) holds 7 NCD mice but 6 HFD mice, where the Fig. 2 legend says 7. The sex of MPK173 and MPK182 differs between their first and second phase files. MPK173 has one 60-trial session in cohort 2; it is left out of the 90-trial analyses. The age is "P12W/" in every file, which cannot be right for recordings that span a year (the diet switch happens at about 21 weeks, Fig. 3a).

def sel_c1(min_trig=30):
    return R[(R.phase == "first") & (R.cohort == 1) & (R.n_triggered >= min_trig)]

def sel_c2(min_trig=30):
    return R[(R.phase == "first") & (R.cohort == 2) & (R.n_trials >= 89) & (R.n_triggered >= min_trig)]

def sel_switch(phase, min_trig=30):
    return R[R.switch.notna() & (R.phase == phase) & (R.n_triggered >= min_trig)]

def count(df, by):
    return df.groupby(by).agg(recordings=("path", "size"), mice=("subject", "nunique"))

The groups of the diet switch are the same mice as cohorts 1 and 2: the first-diet recordings are their cohort recordings, and the second-diet recordings are separate files whose notes give startdiet and 2nd_diet. The first-diet counts match the Fig. 3 legend for NCD->NCD (44) and fall short by 1 to 5 for the others; the second-diet counts match it for NCD->NCD (43), NCD->HFD6w (36) and HFD->HFD (23), and are one short for HFD->NCD (41 against 42). The diet-switch groups mix 60-trial sessions (cohort 1 mice) with 90-trial sessions (cohort 2 mice), where the claims file describes 90-trial sessions.

The trial matrices have 3001 samples, 60 s at 50 Hz, as the Methods' 60-s trials; the starting_time rate is stored as 1 Hz in about half the files and 50 Hz in the others, so the stored rate is wrong in about half the files (the raw trace lengths at 50 Hz, 51.7 to 142.7 min with medians of 66 min for 59 and 60 trials and 95 to 96 min for 89 and 90 trials, fit the session lengths of the Methods). The raw trace holds no power above 10 Hz: it is the low-passed trace of the Methods. In 27 files one series has more trial columns than the Ensure matrix (one more in most, 90 against 60 or 46 in two); trials beyond the Ensure matrix are dropped. Running is missing from 9 files, the deposited Z-score from 27 and the raw trace from 6.

The pump signal rises at sample 549 to 552 in every triggered trial, 1 s after the tone, as the Methods' delivery at t = 1 s, so sample 500 is the tone. Untriggered trials have a cue-window lick rate near zero and triggered trials a high one, which shows that the lick matrix shares the clock of the trial structure: a lick in the 1-s cue window triggers delivery (Methods). The Ensure value in the notes is read as mL (range 0 to about 4; 50 uL per triggered trial gives up to 4.5 mL in 90 trials), which is consistent with the data, not shown by them. The notes carry no unit for body weight; the values fit grams.

The raw trace has no tone time stamps. In the files where the deposited Z-score matches the raw trace, the first trial starts at sample 14,750 to 14,773, that is 295 s, so the first tone is 5 min 5 s into the recording (the Methods' 5-min baseline), and every later trial is 3000 samples (60 s) after the previous one, within 3 samples. This is the shared clock of the raw trace and the trial matrices. In 32 files the deposited Z-score does not match the raw trace of the same file at any offset (median correlation below 0.5): the deposited Z-score and the raw trace of these files cannot both come from the same recording, or the Z-score was computed from a differently processed signal. Where that happens, and in the 26 files without a Z-score, the raw measures use the modal offset of the matched files with the same number of trials (58 files; an assumption that the session timing is the same, checked against the tone response in the next cells). The deposited Z-score is used only as a variant (Z0): how it was computed is not described.

The check below tests the trial starts of every recording against the raw trace itself. The tone evokes a fast rise of the raw signal, from about 0.3 s after the tone, in triggered and untriggered trials alike (first lines of the output, from the correlation-aligned files), so the tones can be located in the raw trace without the deposited Z-score (pvh.alignment_check). For each recording: (a) the tone response averaged over its trials, with all tone times shifted together by -30 to 30 s, and the shift at which it peaks; (b) the tone response at the five slots of the 60-s grid before the first trial (inside the 5-min baseline, which holds no tone) against the first five trials, and (b') the same at the five slots after the last trial against the last five trials, where the trace runs on that far.

ok_recs = [r for r in recs if "align_check" in r]
grid = np.arange(-10, 50, 0.1) + 0.05
for src in ["correlation", "modal"]:
    tr = np.nanmean([r["avg_trig"] for r in ok_recs if r["offset_source"] == src and r["avg_trig"] is not None], axis=0)
    un = np.nanmean([r["avg_untrig"] for r in ok_recs if r["offset_source"] == src and r["avg_untrig"] is not None], axis=0)
    at = {t: int(np.argmin(abs(grid - t))) for t in [-1, 0, 0.3, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 5]}
    print(f"{src}-aligned recordings, mean dF/F0 at t (s) after the tone, triggered trials:",
          {t: round(float(tr[i]), 4) for t, i in at.items()})
    print(f"{' ' * len(src)}                   untriggered trials:", {t: round(float(un[i]), 4) for t, i in at.items()})
A = pd.DataFrame([dict(path=r["path"], subject=r["subject"], n_trials=r["n_trials"], n_triggered=int(r["triggered"].sum()),
                       offset_source=r["offset_source"],
                       zscore="none" if "z0" not in r else ("matched" if r.get("z_raw_match") else "not matched"),
                       peak_shift_s=pvh.TONE_LAGS[int(np.nanargmax(r["align_check"]["scan"]))] / pvh.FS,
                       tone_resp_at_0=r["align_check"]["scan"][int(np.argmin(abs(pvh.TONE_LAGS)))],
                       before_first=np.nanmean(r["align_check"]["before"]), first5=np.nanmean(r["align_check"]["first"]),
                       last5=np.nanmean(r["align_check"]["last"]), after_last=np.nanmean(r["align_check"]["after"]),
                       n_after=int(np.isfinite(r["align_check"]["after"]).sum()),
                       raw_after_last_trial_s=r["raw_tail_s"])
                  for r in ok_recs])
A["peak"] = pd.cut(A.peak_shift_s, [-31, -1.0001, 1, 11, 31], labels=["< -1 s", "-1 to 1 s", "1 to 11 s", "> 11 s"])
print("\n(a) Shift at which the tone response peaks, recordings per class:")
print(A.groupby(["offset_source", "peak"], observed=False).size().unstack(fill_value=0).to_string())
print("(b) Tone response larger in the first five trials than in the five slots before them:",
      A.groupby("offset_source").apply(lambda g: f"{int((g.first5 > g.before_first).sum())} of {len(g)}", include_groups=False).to_dict())
for src, g in A.groupby("offset_source"):
    w = stats.wilcoxon(g.first5, g.before_first)
    print(f"    {src}: median before {g.before_first.median():.4f}, first five {g.first5.median():.4f}, Wilcoxon p {w.pvalue:.2g}")
print("(b') Tone response larger in the last five trials than in the slots after them (recordings with all five slots inside the trace):",
      A[A.n_after == 5].groupby("offset_source").apply(lambda g: f"{int((g.last5 > g.after_last).sum())} of {len(g)}", include_groups=False).to_dict())
for src, g in A[A.n_after == 5].groupby("offset_source"):
    print(f"    {src}: median last five {g.last5.median():.4f}, after {g.after_last.median():.4f}")
fail_b = A[(A.offset_source == "modal") & ~(A.first5 > A.before_first)]
print(f"\nThe {len(fail_b)} modal-offset recordings that fail (b), with the slots after the last trial:")
print(fail_b[["path", "n_triggered", "peak_shift_s", "before_first", "first5", "last5", "after_last", "n_after"]]
      .assign(path=lambda d: d.path.str.split("/").str[-1]).to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.4g}"))
print("\nRaw trace after the last trial (s), by offset source:")

As a group, the modal-offset recordings have their tone response where the correlation-aligned ones have it; for single recordings with no measurable tone response the check cannot place the trials. The tone response rises from about 0.3 s after the tone in both groups and in untriggered trials as well. (a) It peaks within 1 s of the trial grid in 218 of 285 correlation-aligned and 40 of 58 modal-offset recordings; most of the others peak 1 to 11 s later (65 and 17), where the consumption response is. That fits a weak tone response under the later consumption response, but the check does not show it. One recording of each group peaks more than 1 s early, and one correlation-aligned recording more than 11 s late; the early modal one, MPK134 2024-05-03, has a weak tone response (0.006 in its first five trials). (b) Before the first trial the tone response is near zero (medians -0.0013 and -0.0002) and in the first five trials it is positive (0.020 and 0.022), larger in 242 of 285 and 49 of 58 recordings. (b') After the last trial it is near zero again (medians 0.0007 and 0.0008, against 0.016 and 0.013 in the last five trials), larger in the last five trials in 47 of 55 and 15 of 16 recordings with all five slots in the trace. In the 9 modal-offset recordings that fail (b) (the four second-phase MPK147 files of 2024-05-21 to 06-05, MPK147 2024-03-15, MPK133 2024-04-15, MPK134 2024-05-13, MPK118 2024-02-08 and MPK174 2024-10-11), the tone response in the first five trials is -0.035 to 0.0001, and in the last five trials it is -0.007 to 0.004 in all but MPK134 2024-05-13 (0.017, against -0.001 after it). For these 9 the check shows no tone response at either end, so it neither confirms nor excludes a shift of their trials. The modal-offset group passes (b) and (b') as a whole. The correlation-aligned recordings also run on for 7 to 2869 s after the last trial, so a long trace does not mean a different start. This is consistent with the modal offset; it cannot exclude an error of under a second in a recording with a weak tone response. The results without the 58 recordings are given at the end, before the summary.

How the deposited Z-score (Z0) relates to the Z2 computed here: per recording, the correlation over triggered trials of the 1-10 s responses, and the slope of Z0 on Z2.

In the 285 files where it matches the raw trace, the deposited Z-score follows Z2 from trial to trial (median r 0.935 over a recording's triggered trials, median slope 0.92, median intercept 0.08; pooled r 0.875 over 16,334 trials). In the 32 files where it does not match, the agreement is weaker (median r 0.79, slopes -0.56 to 3.7). Z0 thus follows the trial-to-trial variation of Z2 in the matched files, but not its level: the per-recording intercepts vary (SD 0.22, -1.06 to 0.66), and these level differences separate Z0 from Z2 (for example NCD early in cohort 1 is -0.17 under Z0 and 0.43 under Z2, 1-10 s, below). The sigma and baseline used for Z0 are not described.

Fig. 1: cohort 1¶

Readings used throughout (claims file, opening comment): response windows W 0-10, 1-10, 1-9 s; Z1 and Z2 as defined there, each with the per-mouse sigma taken over all the mouse's recordings (z1, z2) or over its recordings of the same diet phase (z1p, z2p), two readings of the Methods' "a single Z-score per animal" (see pvh); early = first 15 triggered trials, late = last 15; D5 and D15 for the delta Z-score. Z0, the depositors' Z-score, and dF/F0 are shown as variants and do not decide outcomes. For cohort 1 and 2 claims Z1p and Z2p use only the first-diet recordings.

In [12]:
ZS, ZV = ["z1", "z2", "z1p", "z2p"], ["z0"]
W1 = ["0-10", "1-10", "1-9"]

def means(df, z, w, phases=("early", "late"), by="diet"):
    cols = [f"{z}|{w}|{p}" for p in phases]
    g = df.groupby(by)[cols]
    out = pd.concat({"mean": g.mean(), "sem": g.sem(), "n": g.count()}, axis=1)
    out.columns = [f"{a}_{b.split('|')[-1]}" for a, b in out.columns]
    return out

def mouse_table(df, cols, by="diet"):
    return df.groupby([by, "subject"])[cols].mean().reset_index()

fig1k-early-late-recordings¶

Per recording, PVH MC4R consumption responses in NCD mice are small early in the meal (Z 0.12 +- 0.11) and larger late (0.86 +- 0.09); in HFD mice they are already high early (0.72 +- 0.09) and do not increase late (0.79 +- 0.09).

In [13]:
EXP_1K = {("NCD", "early"): (0.12, 0.11), ("NCD", "late"): (0.86, 0.09),
          ("HFD", "early"): (0.72, 0.09), ("HFD", "late"): (0.79, 0.09)}
c1 = sel_c1()


def run_f1k(c1):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV + ["dff"]:
        for w in W1:
            m = means(c1, z, w)
            row = {"Z": z, "W": w}
            inside = []
            for (d, p), (v, tol) in EXP_1K.items():
                row[f"{d} {p}"] = m.loc[d, f"mean_{p}"]
                row[f"{d} {p} sem"] = m.loc[d, f"sem_{p}"]
                inside.append(abs(m.loc[d, f"mean_{p}"] - v) <= tol)
            row["n in tolerance"] = sum(inside)
            row["all four"] = all(inside)
            row["NCD late > NCD early"] = row["NCD late"] > row["NCD early"]
            row["HFD early > NCD early"] = row["HFD early"] > row["NCD early"]
            rows.append(row)
    F1K = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return F1K

F1K = run_f1k(c1)

Result: partially reproduced. No combination of window and Z reading puts all four means within tolerance; the best put two in (Z2 and Z2p: HFD early 0.72 to 0.80 and HFD late 0.73 to 0.82 against 0.72 and 0.79, while NCD early is 0.33 to 0.43 against 0.12 +- 0.11 and NCD late 1.01 to 1.22 against 0.86 +- 0.09). Under every combination NCD late is above NCD early and HFD early is above NCD early, which is the partial condition. Under Z1 and Z1p every value is smaller (NCD early 0.10 to 0.13, late 0.38 to 0.43). The depositors' Z-score (Z0, a variant) gives NCD early -0.17 to -0.23, also outside tolerance.

fig1k-lme¶

In a linear mixed-effects model of recording-level responses with mouse as a random intercept, HFD early-meal responses exceed NCD early-meal responses and the diet by meal-phase interaction is significant.

In [15]:
def lme_diet_phase(df, z, w, group="diet", ref="NCD"):
    long = pd.concat([
        pd.DataFrame({"Value": df[f"{z}|{w}|early"], "Diet": df[group], "Phase": "Early", "Mouse": df.subject}),
        pd.DataFrame({"Value": df[f"{z}|{w}|late"], "Diet": df[group], "Phase": "Late", "Mouse": df.subject})])
    long = long.dropna()
    m = smf.mixedlm(f"Value ~ C(Diet, Treatment('{ref}')) * C(Phase, Treatment('Early'))", long,
                    groups=long["Mouse"]).fit(reml=True)
    return m


def run_lme1(c1):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in W1:
            m = lme_diet_phase(c1, z, w)
            names = m.params.index
            d = [n for n in names if "Diet" in n and ":" not in n][0]
            i = [n for n in names if ":" in n][0]
            rows.append({"Z": z, "W": w, "HFD coef": m.params[d], "p HFD": m.pvalues[d],
                         "interaction": m.params[i], "p interaction": m.pvalues[i],
                         "converged": m.converged})
    LME1 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    LME1["full (p<0.001 both, signs)"] = (LME1["HFD coef"] > 0) & (LME1["p HFD"] < 0.001) & (LME1.interaction < 0) & (LME1["p interaction"] < 0.001)
    LME1["partial (p<0.05 both, signs)"] = (LME1["HFD coef"] > 0) & (LME1["p HFD"] < 0.05) & (LME1.interaction < 0) & (LME1["p interaction"] < 0.05)
    return LME1

LME1 = run_lme1(c1)
print(f"Rows: {2 * len(c1)} (two per recording), mice: {c1.subject.nunique()}")
print(LME1.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"))

Result: not reproduced. The diet by meal-phase interaction is negative with p < 0.001 under every Z1, Z2, Z1p and Z2p combination (p 8e-07 to 1.2e-05), but the HFD coefficient (HFD against NCD early in the meal) is positive with p 0.09 to 0.35, so neither the full nor the partial condition holds. With the depositors' Z-score (Z0, a variant that does not decide the outcome) both hold at p < 0.001 (HFD coefficient 0.80 to 0.88, p 1.3e-06 to 4.7e-06; interaction -0.58 to -0.64, p 4e-05 to 6e-05).

fig1l-early-late-mice¶

Per mouse, every NCD mouse increases its response from early to late in the meal (Z 0.19 +- 0.24 to 0.91 +- 0.13), while HFD mice do not change (0.73 +- 0.19 to 0.80 +- 0.20).

In [16]:
EXP_1L = {("NCD", "early"): (0.19, 0.24), ("NCD", "late"): (0.91, 0.13),
          ("HFD", "early"): (0.73, 0.19), ("HFD", "late"): (0.80, 0.20)}


def run_f1l(c1):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in W1:
            mt = mouse_table(c1, [f"{z}|{w}|early", f"{z}|{w}|late"])
            row = {"Z": z, "W": w}
            inside = []
            for (d, p), (v, tol) in EXP_1L.items():
                x = mt[mt.diet == d][f"{z}|{w}|{p}"]
                row[f"{d} {p}"] = x.mean(); row[f"{d} {p} sem"] = x.sem()
                inside.append(abs(x.mean() - v) <= tol)
            n = mt[mt.diet == "NCD"]
            row["NCD mice late>early"] = f"{int((n[f'{z}|{w}|late'] > n[f'{z}|{w}|early']).sum())}/{len(n)}"
            for d in ["NCD", "HFD"]:
                x = mt[mt.diet == d]
                t = stats.ttest_rel(x[f"{z}|{w}|late"], x[f"{z}|{w}|early"])
                row[f"p {d}"] = t.pvalue
                row[f"{d} late-early"] = (x[f"{z}|{w}|late"] - x[f"{z}|{w}|early"]).mean()
            row["means in tol"] = sum(inside)
            row["tests as claimed"] = (row["NCD mice late>early"] == f"{len(n)}/{len(n)}") and row["p NCD"] < 0.05 and row["p HFD"] >= 0.05
            row["full"] = row["tests as claimed"] and all(inside)
            rows.append(row)
    F1L = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return F1L

supp1i-hfd-no-change-1-20s¶

With a longer response window of 1 to 20 s after the cue, HFD mice still show no change in response from early to late in the meal.

In [17]:
def tukey(values, labels):
    """Tukey HSD over all groups; a table of every pair with unrounded p-values and
    diff = mean(group1) - mean(group2)."""
    import itertools
    tk = pairwise_tukeyhsd(np.asarray(values, float), np.asarray(labels).astype(str))
    pairs = list(itertools.combinations(tk.groupsunique, 2))
    # statsmodels' meandiffs are mean(group2) - mean(group1)
    return pd.DataFrame({"group1": [a for a, _ in pairs], "group2": [b for _, b in pairs],
                         "diff": -np.asarray(tk.meandiffs), "p-adj": tk.pvalues})

def anova_tukey(long, value="Value", f1="A", f2="B"):
    import statsmodels.api as sm
    model = smf.ols(f"{value} ~ C({f1}) * C({f2})", long).fit()
    table = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
    tkd = tukey(long[value], long[f1].astype(str) + "|" + long[f2].astype(str))
    return table, tkd

def tukey_p(tkd, a, b):
    """Tukey p and mean(a) - mean(b)."""
    r = tkd[((tkd.group1 == a) & (tkd.group2 == b)) | ((tkd.group1 == b) & (tkd.group2 == a))].iloc[0]
    return float(r["p-adj"]), float(r["diff"]) * (1 if r.group1 == a else -1)


def run_s1i(c1):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in ["0-20", "1-20"]:
            mt = mouse_table(c1, [f"{z}|{w}|early", f"{z}|{w}|late"])
            long = pd.concat([pd.DataFrame({"Value": mt[f"{z}|{w}|{p}"], "A": mt.diet, "B": p}) for p in ["early", "late"]])
            tab, tkd = anova_tukey(long)
            ph, dh = tukey_p(tkd, "HFD|late", "HFD|early")
            pn, dn = tukey_p(tkd, "NCD|late", "NCD|early")
            rows.append({"Z": z, "W": w, "HFD early": mt[mt.diet == "HFD"][f"{z}|{w}|early"].mean(),
                         "HFD late": mt[mt.diet == "HFD"][f"{z}|{w}|late"].mean(),
                         "HFD late-early": dh, "Tukey p HFD": ph, "NCD late-early": dn, "Tukey p NCD": pn,
                         "p interaction (ANOVA)": tab.loc["C(A):C(B)", "PR(>F)"]})
    S1I = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S1I

S1I = run_s1i(c1)
print("Mice:", count(c1, "diet").mice.to_dict())

supp1h-dff-early-late¶

Expressed as dF/F, HFD mice have stronger consumption responses than NCD mice at the start of the meal, and these persist to the end of the feeding bout.

In [18]:
def run_s1h(c1):
    rows = []
    for w in W1:
        m = means(c1, "dff", w)
        he, hl, ne = m.loc["HFD", "mean_early"], m.loc["HFD", "mean_late"], m.loc["NCD", "mean_early"]
        rows.append({"W": w, "NCD early": ne, "NCD late": m.loc["NCD", "mean_late"], "HFD early": he,
                     "HFD early sem": m.loc["HFD", "sem_early"], "HFD late": hl,
                     "HFD early > NCD early": he > ne, "HFD late >= HFD early - sem": hl >= he - m.loc["HFD", "sem_early"],
                     "effect HFD-NCD early": he - ne})
    S1H = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S1H

supp1cd-licking-declines¶

Both NCD and HFD mice reduce their licking from the early to the late phase of the session.

In [21]:
def lick_auc(df, norm, win):
    """Per recording, the early and late mean lick-rate curves (1-s bins, -10 to 50 s) over
    triggered trials; per mouse the mean over its recordings; AUC over the window of the curve
    normalized to the mean rate of the 10 s before the tone, by subtraction or division."""
    out = []
    for _, row in df.iterrows():
        r = by_path[row.path]
        L = r["lick_1s"][:, :len(r["triggered"])][:, r["triggered"][:r["lick_1s"].shape[1]]]
        for p, cols in [("early", L[:, :15]), ("late", L[:, -15:])]:
            out.append({"subject": row.subject, "diet": row.diet, "phase": p, **{f"b{i}": v for i, v in enumerate(cols.mean(axis=1))}})
    c = pd.DataFrame(out).groupby(["diet", "subject", "phase"]).mean().reset_index()
    B = c[[f"b{i}" for i in range(60)]].to_numpy()
    base = B[:, :10].mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
    lo, hi = {"1-10": (11, 20), "0-50": (10, 60)}[win]
    seg = B[:, lo:hi]
    c["auc"] = (seg - base).sum(axis=1) if norm == "subtract" else (seg / base).sum(axis=1)
    c["base"] = base[:, 0]
    return c[["diet", "subject", "phase", "auc", "base"]]

rows = []
for norm in ["subtract", "divide"]:
    for win in ["1-10", "0-50"]:
        c = lick_auc(c1, norm, win)
        for d in ["NCD", "HFD"]:
            x = c[c.diet == d].pivot(index="subject", columns="phase", values="auc")
            for test in ["unpaired", "paired"]:
                t = stats.ttest_ind(x.late, x.early) if test == "unpaired" else stats.ttest_rel(x.late, x.early)
                rows.append({"norm": norm, "AUC window": win, "diet": d, "test": test,
                             "early": x.early.mean(), "late": x.late.mean(), "late-early": (x.late - x.early).mean(),
                             "t": t.statistic, "p": t.pvalue, "finite": bool(np.isfinite(x.to_numpy()).all()),
                             "late<early, p<0.05": (x.late.mean() < x.early.mean()) and t.pvalue < 0.05})

Result: blocked (methods underspecified). The readings disagree. With the AUC normalized by subtracting the pre-tone lick rate, late is below early with p < 0.05 in both diets under both windows and both tests (p 0.0001 to 0.031). With division by the pre-tone rate, late is above early in both diets (p 0.31 to 0.78), because the pre-tone rate falls from early to late (for example MPK134 0.132 to 0.037 licks/s). The criterion blocks the claim when the readings disagree.

def pearson(x, y):
    ok = np.isfinite(x) & np.isfinite(y)
    r, p = stats.pearsonr(x[ok], y[ok])
    return r, p, int(ok.sum())

    F2C = pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: reproduced. Under Z2 (1-9 s, D15) the delta Z-score is 0.61 +- 0.07 for NCD and 0.20 +- 0.06 for HFD recordings, both within tolerance, with NCD above HFD (p 5.4e-05); Z2p (1-9 and 1-10 s, D15) also puts both in. Under the Methods' D5 the HFD value is negative (-0.07 to -0.02) and out of tolerance; under Z1 and Z1p both values are out (NCD 0.10 to 0.17). Every combination gives NCD above HFD with p < 0.001. The outcome rests on an assumption: it holds only with the 58 modal-offset recordings (13 of the 104 here), whose trial starts are taken from the other files. Without them HFD is 0.20 to 0.23 and the claim would be partially reproduced (section before the summary). They are kept because the cohort-2 modal-offset recordings used here pass the tone check as a group.

Result: reproduced. Under Z2 (1-10 s, D15) the per-mouse delta Z-score is 0.61 +- 0.11 for NCD and 0.20 +- 0.10 for HFD mice (7 and 6 mice), both within tolerance, with p 0.020. It is the only Z1 to Z2p combination that puts both in; every one gives NCD above HFD with p < 0.05 (0.008 to 0.030).

fig2e-lick-vigor¶

Throughout the 90-trial meal NCD mice lick at a higher rate during the cue than HFD mice; NCD licking begins to decline after about 50 trials and HFD licking after about 20.

In [27]:
def curve_by_mouse(df, key, n=90):
    """Mean over mice of each mouse's mean over recordings of the per-trial-index value
    (triggered trials only)."""
    M = pvh.per_trial_index(recs, df.path.tolist(), key, n)
    per_mouse = pd.DataFrame(M).groupby(df.subject.to_numpy()).mean()
    return per_mouse.mean(axis=0).to_numpy(), per_mouse

def onset(curve, k=15):
    s = pd.Series(curve).rolling(k, center=True, min_periods=1).mean().to_numpy()
    i_max = int(np.nanargmax(s)) + 1
    base = np.nanmean(curve[:k])
    below = s < base
    j = None
    for i in range(len(s)):
        rest = s[i:][np.isfinite(s[i:])]
        if len(rest) and (rest < base).all():
            j = i + 1
            break
    return i_max, j, s

cn, pm_n = curve_by_mouse(c2[c2.diet == "NCD"], ("lick", "cue"))
ch, pm_h = curve_by_mouse(c2[c2.diet == "HFD"], ("lick", "cue"))
both = np.isfinite(cn) & np.isfinite(ch)
print("Trial indices with data in both groups:", int(both.sum()), "of 90")
print("(a) NCD above HFD at every such index:", bool((cn[both] > ch[both]).all()),
      f"; indices where NCD <= HFD: {(np.where(both & (cn <= ch))[0] + 1).tolist()}")
blocks = [(i, i + 15) for i in range(0, 90, 15)]
bl = [(f"{a + 1}-{b}", np.nanmean(cn[a:b]), np.nanmean(ch[a:b])) for a, b in blocks]
print("(b) 15-trial blocks (NCD, HFD):", [(l, round(x, 2), round(y, 2)) for l, x, y in bl],
      "; NCD above in every block:", all(x > y for _, x, y in bl))
for name, c in [("NCD", cn), ("HFD", ch)]:
    i_max, j, s = onset(c)
    print(f"{name}: (i) index of the maximum of the 15-trial moving mean = {i_max}; "
          f"(ii) first index after which the moving mean stays below the mean of trials 1-15 = {j}; "
          f"mean of trials 1-15 = {np.nanmean(c[:15]):.2f} licks/s")
print("Expected onsets: NCD 50 +- 5, HFD 20 +- 2.")
print("\nMice contributing per trial index (NCD, HFD) at 1, 30, 60, 90:",
      [(i, int(pm_n[i - 1].notna().sum()), int(pm_h[i - 1].notna().sum())) for i in [1, 30, 60, 90]])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3))
ax.plot(np.arange(1, 91), cn, label="NCD"); ax.plot(np.arange(1, 91), ch, label="HFD")
ax.set_xlabel("trial"); ax.set_ylabel("cue lick rate (licks/s)"); ax.legend()
print(f"Plotted ranges: NCD {np.nanmin(cn):.2f} to {np.nanmax(cn):.2f}, HFD {np.nanmin(ch):.2f} to {np.nanmax(ch):.2f}")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()

fig2km-elevated-early-at-matched-licking¶

In sessions of 45 to 74 triggered trials, where early licking vigor is comparable between groups, HFD mice still have larger PVH MC4R responses early in the meal than NCD mice.

def run_f2km(c2_15):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in W2:
            for b in ["45-59", "60-74"]:
                x = c2_15[c2_15.meal_bin == b]
                col = f"{z}|{w}|early"
                n, h = x[x.diet == "NCD"][col].dropna(), x[x.diet == "HFD"][col].dropna()
                ln, lh = x[x.diet == "NCD"]["lick_cue|early"], x[x.diet == "HFD"]["lick_cue|early"]
                rows.append({"Z": z, "W": w, "group": b, "n": f"{len(n)}/{len(h)}", "NCD resp": n.mean(), "HFD resp": h.mean(),
                             "diff": h.mean() - n.mean(), "sum sem": n.sem() + h.sem(),
                             "resp HFD>NCD by > sum sem": h.mean() - n.mean() > n.sem() + h.sem(),
                             "NCD lick": ln.mean(), "HFD lick": lh.mean(), "lick |diff|": abs(lh.mean() - ln.mean()),
                             "lick sum sem": ln.sem() + lh.sem(),
                             "lick comparable": abs(lh.mean() - ln.mean()) < ln.sem() + lh.sem()})
    F2KM = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    F2KM["both"] = F2KM["resp HFD>NCD by > sum sem"] & F2KM["lick comparable"]
    return F2KM

def run_f2q(sel_c2):

    F2Q = pd.DataFrame(rows)

        r, p, n = pearson(x.bw.to_numpy(float), x.n_triggered.to_numpy(float))
        rows.append({"min triggered": k, "diet": d, "r": r, "p": p, "n": n})

supp2h-delta-z-meal-size¶

Across sessions, the within-meal change in response correlates with meal size with r = -0.34 (p = 0.012) in NCD mice and r = 0.26 (p = 0.048) in HFD mice. The sentence calls the NCD correlation positive and the HFD one negative, opposite to the printed signs.

In [35]:
def run_s2h(sel_c2):
    rows = []
    for k in [30, 15]:
        x0 = sel_c2(k)
        for z in ZS + ZV:
            for w in W2:
                for D in ["D15", "D5"]:
                    res = {"min triggered": k, "Z": z, "W": w, "D": D}
                    for d in ["NCD", "HFD"]:
                        x = x0[x0.diet == d]
                        r, p, n = pearson(x.n_triggered.to_numpy(float), x[f"{z}|{w}|{D}"].to_numpy(float))
                        res[f"r {d}"], res[f"p {d}"], res[f"n {d}"] = r, p, n
                    res["numbers match"] = abs(res["r NCD"] + 0.34) <= 0.034 and abs(res["r HFD"] - 0.26) <= 0.026 and res["p NCD"] < 0.05 and res["p HFD"] < 0.05
                    res["words match"] = res["r NCD"] > 0 and res["r HFD"] < 0 and res["p NCD"] < 0.05 and res["p HFD"] < 0.05
                    rows.append(res)
    S2H = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S2H

The NCD correlations are positive (0.13 to 0.22, p 0.11 to 0.33) and the HFD ones negative (-0.003 to -0.33), the signs of the sentence's words, but the two are never both significant: the HFD correlation reaches p < 0.05 only under Z2p with D5 (r -0.31 and -0.33, p 0.035 and 0.027), where the NCD one has p 0.14 and 0.16.

def run_s2j(sel_c2):

        for w in pvh.ROLL_S:

                r, p, n = pearson(x.bw.to_numpy(float), x[f"rollsd_{w}s"].to_numpy(float))

                             "weak & p<0.05": (abs(r) < 0.5) and p < 0.05})
    S2J = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S2J

supp2lp-fasting-no-effect¶

An additional overnight fast does not significantly alter licking or PVH MC4R response dynamics in either diet group.

In [39]:
print("Recordings by condition (legend: nonfasted NCD 31, fasted NCD 28, nonfasted HFD 31, fasted HFD 23; 7 mice each):")
print(c2.groupby(["diet", "condition"]).agg(recordings=("path", "size"), mice=("subject", "nunique")).to_string())


def run_s2l(c2):
    measures = [("cue lick rate", "lick_cue|all")]
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in W2:
            measures += [(f"early {z} {w}", f"{z}|{w}|early"), (f"D15 {z} {w}", f"{z}|{w}|D15")]
    rows = []
    for d in ["NCD", "HFD"]:
        x = c2[c2.diet == d].copy()
        x["fasted"] = (x.condition == "fasted").astype(int)
        for name, col in measures:
            a, b = x[x.fasted == 1][col].dropna(), x[x.fasted == 0][col].dropna()
            t = stats.ttest_ind(a, b)
            y = x[["fasted", "subject", col]].dropna().rename(columns={col: "v"})
            m = smf.mixedlm("v ~ fasted", y, groups=y.subject).fit(reml=True)
            rows.append({"diet": d, "measure": name, "fasted": a.mean(), "nonfasted": b.mean(), "diff": a.mean() - b.mean(),
                         "p t-test": t.pvalue, "LME coef": m.params["fasted"], "p LME": m.pvalues["fasted"]})
    S2L = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S2L


S2L = run_s2l(c2)
print(S2L.to_string(index=False, float_format=lambda v: f"{v:.3g}"))
for zs, lab in [(ZS, "Z1/Z2 readings"), (ZV, "Z0 variant")]:
    keep = S2L.measure.str.contains("lick") | S2L.measure.str.contains("|".join(zs))
    s = S2L[keep]
    print(f"{lab}: tests with p < 0.05 -- t-test: {int((s['p t-test'] < 0.05).sum())} of {len(s)}, "
          f"LME: {int((s['p LME'] < 0.05).sum())} of {len(s)}")

Z0 variant: tests with p < 0.05 -- t-test: 3 of 10, LME: 3 of 10

Result: not reproduced. Both test readings find an effect of fasting in HFD sessions: the cue lick rate is higher after fasting (4.01 against 3.29 licks/s; t-test p 0.037, LME p 0.005) and the early-meal response is lower under Z2 and Z2p (t-test p 0.007 to 0.024, LME p 0.004 to 0.010; under Z1 and Z1p LME p 0.021 to 0.027). In NCD sessions no test has p < 0.05. The delta Z-score does not differ in either diet.

fig3h-early-response-diet-switch¶

After switching from HFD to NCD, early-meal PVH MC4R responses fall from their level on HFD toward NCD levels, while HFD->HFD mice keep high early-meal responses.

In [42]:
def run_f3h(SW30):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in W2:
            x = SW30[SW30.switch.isin(THREE)]
            col = f"{z}|{w}|early"
            long = x[["switch", "phase_label", col]].dropna().rename(columns={col: "Value", "switch": "A", "phase_label": "B"})
            tab, tkd = anova_tukey(long)
            p1, d1 = tukey_p(tkd, "HFD->NCD|after", "HFD->NCD|before")
            p2, d2 = tukey_p(tkd, "HFD->HFD|after", "HFD->HFD|before")
            p3, d3 = tukey_p(tkd, "HFD->NCD|before", "NCD->NCD|before")
            p4, d4 = tukey_p(tkd, "HFD->HFD|before", "NCD->NCD|before")
            g = long.groupby(["A", "B"]).Value.mean()
            rows.append({"Z": z, "W": w, "HFD->NCD before": g[("HFD->NCD", "before")], "HFD->NCD after": g[("HFD->NCD", "after")],
                         "after-before HFD->NCD": d1, "Tukey p": p1,
                         "HFD->HFD before": g[("HFD->HFD", "before")], "HFD->HFD after": g[("HFD->HFD", "after")],
                         "after-before HFD->HFD": d2, "Tukey p HH": p2,
                         "NCD->NCD before": g[("NCD->NCD", "before")], "NCD->NCD after": g[("NCD->NCD", "after")],
                         "HN-NN before": d3, "p HN-NN": p3, "HH-NN before": d4, "p HH-NN": p4})
    F3H = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    F3H["full"] = (F3H["after-before HFD->NCD"] < 0) & (F3H["Tukey p"] < 0.05) & ~((F3H["after-before HFD->HFD"] < 0) & (F3H["Tukey p HH"] < 0.05))
    return F3H

fig3i-ncd-increase-only¶

After the diet switch, NCD->NCD mice show a significant increase in response from early to late in the meal, while HFD->NCD mice show only a slight, nonsignificant increase.

In [43]:
x2 = SW30[(SW30.phase == "second") & SW30.switch.isin(THREE)]


def run_f3i(x2):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in W2:
            res = {"Z": z, "W": w}
            for ref in THREE:
                m = lme_diet_phase(x2, z, w, group="switch", ref=ref)
                k = [n for n in m.params.index if "Phase" in n and ":" not in n][0]
                res[f"LME late-early {ref}"] = m.params[k]; res[f"p LME {ref}"] = m.pvalues[k]
            mt = mouse_table(x2, [f"{z}|{w}|early", f"{z}|{w}|late"], by="switch")
            for g in THREE:
                y = mt[mt.switch == g]
                t = stats.ttest_rel(y[f"{z}|{w}|late"], y[f"{z}|{w}|early"])
                res[f"paired diff {g}"] = (y[f"{z}|{w}|late"] - y[f"{z}|{w}|early"]).mean(); res[f"p paired {g}"] = t.pvalue
            rows.append(res)
    F3I = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    F3I["NN increase (both p<0.05)"] = (F3I["LME late-early NCD->NCD"] > 0) & (F3I["p LME NCD->NCD"] < 0.05) & (F3I["paired diff NCD->NCD"] > 0) & (F3I["p paired NCD->NCD"] < 0.05)
    F3I["HN absence (neither p<0.05, late>early)"] = (F3I["p LME HFD->NCD"] >= 0.05) & (F3I["p paired HFD->NCD"] >= 0.05) & (F3I["paired diff HFD->NCD"] > 0)
    F3I["HN both tests p<0.05"] = (F3I["p LME HFD->NCD"] < 0.05) & (F3I["p paired HFD->NCD"] < 0.05)
    return F3I

Result: reproduced. Under Z2 and Z2p (both windows), NCD->NCD mice increase from early to late after the switch in the LME (p 0.002 to 0.003) and the paired t-test (p 0.004 to 0.006), and HFD->NCD mice show a small increase that neither test finds significant (LME p 0.40 to 0.60, paired p 0.14 to 0.35). fig3j-delta-z-diet-switch¶

After the switch, the per-mouse early-to-late change in response is 0.37 +- 0.03 in NCD->NCD, 0.14 +- 0.05 in HFD->NCD and -0.05 +- 0.07 in HFD->HFD mice; it is significantly smaller in HFD->HFD.

In [44]:
EXP_3J = {"NCD->NCD": (0.37, 0.03), "HFD->NCD": (0.14, 0.05), "HFD->HFD": (-0.05, 0.07)}


def run_f3j(x2):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in W2:
            for D in ["D5", "D15"]:
                col = f"{z}|{w}|{D}"
                mt = x2.groupby(["switch", "subject"])[col].mean().reset_index().dropna()
                groups = [mt[mt.switch == g][col] for g in THREE]
                an = stats.f_oneway(*groups)
                tkd = tukey(mt[col], mt.switch)
                p, d = tukey_p(tkd, "HFD->HFD", "NCD->NCD")
                res = {"Z": z, "W": w, "D": D}
                inside = []
                for g in THREE:
                    v = mt[mt.switch == g][col]
                    res[g] = v.mean(); res[f"{g} sem"] = v.sem()
                    inside.append(abs(v.mean() - EXP_3J[g][0]) <= EXP_3J[g][1])
                res.update({"ANOVA p": an.pvalue, "HH-NN": d, "Tukey p HH-NN": p, "in tol": "".join(str(int(i)) for i in inside),
                            "order NN>HN>HH": res["NCD->NCD"] > res["HFD->NCD"] > res["HFD->HFD"]})
                res["full"] = all(inside) and d < 0 and p < 0.05
                res["partial"] = res["order NN>HN>HH"] and d < 0 and p < 0.05
                rows.append(res)
    F3J = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return F3J

F3J = run_f3j(x2)

supp3c-ncd-hfd6w-dynamics-retained¶

NCD mice switched to HFD for 6 weeks keep their response dynamics, with a significant early-to-late increase in response after the switch, comparable to the change before it, and stable licking vigor.

In [48]:
nh = SW30[SW30.switch == "NCD->HFD6w"]


def run_s3c(nh):
    rows = []
    for z in ZS + ZV:
        for w in ["1-9", "1-19"]:
            res = {"Z": z, "W": w}
            for ph, lab in [("first", "NCD"), ("second", "HFD6w")]:
                mt = mouse_table(nh[nh.phase == ph], [f"{z}|{w}|early", f"{z}|{w}|late"], by="switch")
                t = stats.ttest_rel(mt[f"{z}|{w}|late"], mt[f"{z}|{w}|early"])
                res[f"{lab} early"] = mt[f"{z}|{w}|early"].mean(); res[f"{lab} late"] = mt[f"{z}|{w}|late"].mean()
                res[f"{lab} p"] = t.pvalue; res[f"{lab} n mice"] = len(mt)
            res["both phases late>early p<0.05"] = (res["NCD late"] > res["NCD early"]) and res["NCD p"] < 0.05 and (res["HFD6w late"] > res["HFD6w early"]) and res["HFD6w p"] < 0.05
            res["HFD6w only"] = (res["HFD6w late"] > res["HFD6w early"]) and res["HFD6w p"] < 0.05
            rows.append(res)
    S3C = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S3C

supp3m-weight-gain-response¶

In the second diet phase, mid-meal responses correlate positively with weight gain in NCD->HFD6w mice (r = 0.53, p = 0.001) and also in NCD->NCD mice (r = 0.46, p = 0.003).

In [50]:
def run_s3m(SW):
    rows = []
    for k in [30, 15]:
        x0 = SW[(SW.phase == "second") & (SW.n_triggered >= k)].copy()
        x0["C-A"] = x0.bw - x0.before_adlib_bw
        x0["C/A"] = x0.bw / x0.before_adlib_bw
        for z in ZS + ZV:
            for w in W2:
                for gain in ["C-A", "C/A"]:
                    res = {"min triggered": k, "Z": z, "W": w, "gain": gain}
                    for g, (rr, tol) in {"NCD->HFD6w": (0.53, 0.053), "NCD->NCD": (0.46, 0.046)}.items():
                        x = x0[x0.switch == g]
                        r, p, n = pearson(x[gain].to_numpy(float), x[f"{z}|{w}|mid"].to_numpy(float))
                        res[f"r {g}"], res[f"p {g}"], res[f"n {g}"] = r, p, n
                        res[f"tol {g}"] = abs(r - rr) <= tol and p < 0.05
                    rows.append(res)
    S3M = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S3M

supp3q-hfd-ncd-weight-loss-meal-length¶

In HFD->NCD mice, meal length correlates negatively with weight change, so mice that lost more weight before the session tended to eat larger meals; neural responses do not correlate with weight change.

In [52]:
def run_s3q(SW30):
    x0 = SW30[(SW30.phase == "second") & (SW30.switch == "HFD->NCD")].copy()
    readings = {"C-B (max ad lib)": x0.bw - x0.adlib_bw, "C/B (max ad lib)": x0.bw / x0.adlib_bw,
                "C-A (start of ad lib, legend)": x0.bw - x0.before_adlib_bw, "C/A (start of ad lib, legend)": x0.bw / x0.before_adlib_bw}
    rows = []
    for name, wc in readings.items():
        r1, p1, n1 = pearson(wc.to_numpy(float), x0.n_triggered.to_numpy(float))
        res = {"weight change": name, "r meal length": r1, "p meal length": p1, "n": n1}
        worst_i, worst_ii = 1.0, 1.0
        for z in ZS:
            for w in W2:
                ri, pi, _ = pearson(wc.to_numpy(float), x0[f"{z}|{w}|mid"].to_numpy(float))
                rii, pii, _ = pearson(x0.n_triggered.to_numpy(float), x0[f"{z}|{w}|mid"].to_numpy(float))
                res[f"r(i) {z} {w}"], res[f"p(i) {z} {w}"] = ri, pi
                res[f"r(ii) {z} {w}"], res[f"p(ii) {z} {w}"] = rii, pii
                worst_i, worst_ii = min(worst_i, pi), min(worst_ii, pii)
        res["min p (i)"], res["min p (ii)"] = worst_i, worst_ii
        rows.append(res)
    S3Q = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return S3Q, x0, readings


S3Q, x0, readings = run_s3q(SW30)

def s3q_decision(S3Q):
    """The criterion per weight-change reading and per Z and W combination: meal length r < 0
    with p < 0.05, and the neural correlations (i) and (ii) with p >= 0.05."""
    rows = []
    for _, s in S3Q.iterrows():
        for z in ZS:
            for w in W2:
                first = s["r meal length"] < 0 and s["p meal length"] < 0.05
                a, b = s[f"p(i) {z} {w}"] >= 0.05, s[f"p(ii) {z} {w}"] >= 0.05
                rows.append({"weight change": s["weight change"], "Z": z, "W": w, "meal length r<0, p<0.05": first,
                             "(i) p>=0.05": a, "(ii) p>=0.05": b,
                             "decision": "reproduced" if first and a and b else
                                         "partial" if first and (a or b) else "neither"})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: partially reproduced (assumed). In HFD->NCD second-phase recordings, meal size correlates negatively with the weight on the day relative to ad lib bw (read as B, the maximal ad libitum weight) as a ratio (r -0.35, p 0.023); as a difference, and relative to before ad lib bw (read as A, the legend's reading), r is -0.24 to -0.27 (p 0.09 to 0.14), so only C/B meets the first condition. Under C/B the mid-meal response correlates with neither weight change (p 0.64 to 0.998) nor, under Z2, Z1p and Z2p, meal size (p 0.08 to 0.35), the full condition (6 of 8 Z and W combinations); under Z1 it correlates with meal size (r -0.32, p 0.039 and 0.043), so only (i) is absent, the partial condition (2 of 8). The neural part of the claim is a claim of absence, and one of the claims file's Z readings finds the effect, so the outcome is partially reproduced. It rests on reading ad lib bw as B.

Alignment check: results without the modal-offset recordings¶

The raw measures (Z1, Z2, Z1p, Z2p, dF/F0, the pre-Ensure variability) of 58 recordings use the modal trial offset, not one found by correlation (data check above). The tone check above finds their tone response where it is in the correlation-aligned files as a group, and cannot place 9 of them, which show no tone response. Here every analysis that uses the raw trace is run again on the recordings whose trial starts were found by correlation only; each per-mouse sigma is left as computed from all of the mouse's recordings. The table gives, for each claim, the numbers its outcome rests on, with all recordings and without the 58.

In [53]:
Rc = R[R.offset_source != "modal"].copy()


def sel_c1x(min_trig=30):
    return Rc[(Rc.phase == "first") & (Rc.cohort == 1) & (Rc.n_triggered >= min_trig)]


def sel_c2x(min_trig=30):
    return Rc[(Rc.phase == "first") & (Rc.cohort == 2) & (Rc.n_trials >= 89) & (Rc.n_triggered >= min_trig)]


SWx = Rc[Rc.switch.notna()].copy()
SWx["phase_label"] = np.where(SWx.phase == "first", "before", "after")
SW30x = SWx[SWx.n_triggered >= 30]
x2x = SW30x[(SW30x.phase == "second") & SW30x.switch.isin(THREE)]
print("Recordings left out (modal offset), by group, of those each analysis uses:")
print(f"  cohort 1 (>= 30 triggered): {len(c1) - len(sel_c1x())} of {len(c1)}; "
      f"cohort 2 (>= 30): {len(c2) - len(sel_c2x())} of {len(c2)}; (>= 15): {len(c2_15) - len(sel_c2x(15))} of {len(c2_15)}")
print("  diet switch (>= 30 triggered):",
      (count(SW30, ["switch", "phase_label"]).recordings - count(SW30x, ["switch", "phase_label"]).recordings).to_dict())


def run_all(c1, c2, c2_15, sel_c2, SW, SW30, x2):
    return {"F1K": run_f1k(c1), "LME1": run_lme1(c1), "F1L": run_f1l(c1), "S1I": run_s1i(c1), "S1H": run_s1h(c1),
            "F2C": run_f2c(c2), "F2D": run_f2d(c2), "F2KM": run_f2km(c2_15), "F2Q": run_f2q(sel_c2),
            "F2R": run_f2r(sel_c2), "S2H": run_s2h(sel_c2), "S2J": run_s2j(sel_c2), "S2K": run_s2k(c2),
            "S2L": run_s2l(c2), "F3H": run_f3h(SW30), "F3I": run_f3i(x2), "F3J": run_f3j(x2),
            "S3C": run_s3c(SW30[SW30.switch == "NCD->HFD6w"]), "S3M": run_s3m(SW),
            "S3QD": s3q_decision(run_s3q(SW30)[0])}


def summaries(T):
    """The numbers each outcome rests on, under the claims file's readings (Z1, Z2, Z1p, Z2p)."""
    zs = lambda df: df[df.Z.isin(ZS)]
    f, g = lambda v: f"{v:.3g}", lambda s: f"{s.min():.3g} to {s.max():.3g}"
    a = zs(T["F1K"]); b = zs(T["LME1"]); c = zs(T["F1L"]); d = zs(T["S1I"]); e = T["S1H"]
    out = {
        "fig1k-early-late-recordings": f"max means in tol {a['n in tolerance'].max()}/4; partial condition in "
            f"{int((a['NCD late > NCD early'] & a['HFD early > NCD early']).sum())}/{len(a)}",
        "fig1k-lme": f"p HFD {g(b['p HFD'])}; p interaction {g(b['p interaction'])}; partial in {int(b['partial (p<0.05 both, signs)'].sum())}/{len(b)}",
        "fig1l-early-late-mice": f"max means in tol {c['means in tol'].max()}/4; tests as claimed in {int(c['tests as claimed'].sum())}/{len(c)}",
        "supp1i-hfd-no-change-1-20s": f"Tukey p HFD early-late {g(d['Tukey p HFD'])}",
        "supp1h-dff-early-late": f"HFD early > NCD early in {int(e['HFD early > NCD early'].sum())}/3, "
            f"HFD late >= early - sem in {int(e['HFD late >= HFD early - sem'].sum())}/3",
    }
    for key, name in [("F2C", "fig2c-delta-z-recordings"), ("F2D", "fig2d-delta-z-mice")]:
        x = zs(T[key]); ok = (x["in tol"] == "11") & x["NCD>HFD p<0.05"]
        z2 = x[x.Z.isin(["z2", "z2p"]) & (x.D == "D15")]
        out[name] = f"both in tol with p < 0.05 in {int(ok.sum())}/{len(x)} ({', '.join(x[ok].Z + ' ' + x[ok].W + ' ' + x[ok].D)}); " \
                    f"NCD > HFD p < 0.05 in {int(x['NCD>HFD p<0.05'].sum())}/{len(x)}; Z2, Z2p with D15, NCD/HFD: " + \
                    "; ".join(f"{r.Z} {r.W} {r.NCD:.3f}/{r.HFD:.3f}" for r in z2.itertuples())
    x = zs(T["F2KM"]); both = x.groupby(["Z", "W"]).both.all()
    out["fig2km-elevated-early-at-matched-licking"] = f"both groups hold in {int(both.sum())}/{len(both)} Z, W combinations"
    x = zs(T["F2Q"]); h = x[x.diet == "HFD"]
    ok = h["in tol (HFD)"].astype(bool) & (h.p < 0.05)
    out["fig2q-midmeal-response-meal-size"] = f"HFD r {g(h.r)}; in tol with p < 0.05 in {int(ok.sum())}/{len(h)}"
    x = zs(T["F2R"]); h = x[x.diet == "HFD"]
    out["fig2r-weight-midmeal-response"] = f"HFD r {g(h.r)}, p {g(h.p)}"
    x = zs(T["S2H"])
    out["supp2h-delta-z-meal-size"] = f"numbers match in {int(x['numbers match'].sum())}/{len(x)}, words match in {int(x['words match'].sum())}/{len(x)}"
    x = T["S2J"]; h = x[x.diet == "HFD"]
    out["supp2j-variability-weight"] = f"HFD r {g(h.r)}, p {g(h.p)}"
    x = zs(T["S2K"])
    out["supp2k-sex-early-response"] = f"F > M in both diets and larger in HFD in {int((x['F>M both'] & x['larger in HFD']).sum())}/{len(x)}"
    x = T["S2L"]; h = x[(x.diet == "HFD") & (x.measure.str.contains("lick") | x.measure.str.contains("early z"))]
    out["supp2lp-fasting-no-effect"] = f"HFD, lick rate and early response: t-test p < 0.05 in {int((h['p t-test'] < 0.05).sum())}/{len(h)}, LME in {int((h['p LME'] < 0.05).sum())}/{len(h)}"
    x = zs(T["F3H"])
    out["fig3h-early-response-diet-switch"] = f"HFD->NCD after-before {g(x['after-before HFD->NCD'])}, Tukey p {g(x['Tukey p'])}; full in {int(x.full.sum())}/{len(x)}"
    x = zs(T["F3I"]); ok = x["NN increase (both p<0.05)"] & x["HN absence (neither p<0.05, late>early)"]
    out["fig3i-ncd-increase-only"] = f"NN increase and HN absence in {int(ok.sum())}/{len(x)} ({', '.join(x[ok].Z + ' ' + x[ok].W)})"
    x = zs(T["F3J"])
    out["fig3j-delta-z-diet-switch"] = f"Tukey p HH-NN {g(x['Tukey p HH-NN'])}; full {int(x.full.sum())}, partial {int(x.partial.sum())} of {len(x)}"
    x = zs(T["S3C"])
    out["supp3c-ncd-hfd6w-dynamics-retained"] = f"both phases late > early with p < 0.05 in {int(x['both phases late>early p<0.05'].sum())}/{len(x)}; HFD6w p {g(x['HFD6w p'])}"
    x = zs(T["S3M"]); x = x[x["min triggered"] == 30]
    out["supp3m-weight-gain-response"] = f">= 30 triggered: both in tol in {int((x['tol NCD->HFD6w'] & x['tol NCD->NCD']).sum())}/{len(x)}, " \
        f"both r > 0 with p < 0.05 in {int(((x['r NCD->HFD6w'] > 0) & (x['p NCD->HFD6w'] < 0.05) & (x['r NCD->NCD'] > 0) & (x['p NCD->NCD'] < 0.05)).sum())}/{len(x)}"
    out["supp3q-hfd-ncd-weight-loss-meal-length"] = str(T["S3QD"].decision.value_counts().to_dict())
    return out

Without the 58 modal-offset recordings (6 of the 70 cohort 1 and 13 of the 104 cohort 2 recordings with at least 30 triggered trials, 31 of the diet-switch ones) the numbers each outcome rests on change little, and the outcome they give is the same for every claim but one.

  • fig2c-delta-z-recordings: the HFD delta Z-score rises to 0.20 to 0.23 under Z2 and Z2p with D15 (NCD 0.54 to 0.56), so no combination keeps both means within tolerance; NCD is still above HFD with p < 0.05 in all 16 combinations. Without these recordings the outcome would be partially reproduced. With all recordings, which the tone check supports as a group, it stays reproduced; the outcome is marked as assumed.
  • fig2d-delta-z-mice holds in 4 combinations instead of 1; supp2k-sex-early-response holds in 5 of 8 combinations instead of 8; supp3q-hfd-ncd-weight-loss-meal-length gives the full condition in 4 combinations and the partial one in 4, against 6 and 2.
  • fig1k-lme: the HFD coefficient is still not significant (p 0.077 to 0.41).
  • supp2lp-fasting-no-effect: fasting still has effects in HFD (LME p < 0.05 in 9 of 11 tests).
  • fig3h-early-response-diet-switch: the HFD->NCD drop is smaller (Tukey p 0.715 to 1).

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The Z-score of the paper could not be rebuilt exactly: the claims file gives two readings of the Methods' per-animal Z-score (Z1, Z2), run here from the deposited raw 465 nm trace, with the per-mouse SD over all recordings or over one diet phase. The trial onsets in the raw trace are found from the deposited Z-score (or, in 58 files, taken as the modal onset; a check on the tone response supports these onsets for the 58 as a group, and cannot place 9 of them that show no tone response; and without these files every outcome is the same except fig2c, which would be partially reproduced). Trials with a lost signal (12, in two MPK120 recordings) are left out of the raw measures. Speed is the absolute value of the signed running signal. For the claims whose criterion leaves a recording set open, both sets are shown. One cohort-2 HFD mouse of seven, and a few recordings of others, are not in the dataset (counts above).

What was found about the dataset.

  • Four ses-None files are byte-identical copies of dated files (MPK118 2024-02-13, MPK133 2024-02-07, MPK134 2024-02-12, MPK172 2024-07-25); two other ses-None files are unique sessions with no date in the file name.
  • Cohort 2 holds 6 HFD mice, where the paper has 7 (54 recordings); 47 HFD recordings with at least 30 triggered trials are in it. Cohort 1 has one recording fewer than the paper per diet (38 and 32 against 39 and 33).
  • In 32 files the deposited Z-score does not match the raw trace of the same file at any offset.
  • The starting_time rate is 1 Hz in about half the files, where the data are at 50 Hz.
  • In 27 files one series has more trial columns than the Ensure, lick and running matrices.
  • The sex of MPK173 and MPK182 differs between their first- and second-phase files; the first-phase labels give the paper's sex counts for the female HFD group.
  • The age is "P12W/" in every file. One second-phase file of MPK191 is dated 2024-01-02, before the mouse's first-phase recordings (October 2024).
  • The running signal is signed, with no description of the sign; the body weights, Ensure volume and the ad lib bw and before ad lib bw fields have no units or definitions.
  • The 405 nm control, the training sessions and the home-cage food intake are not in the dataset.
